searches.note: Twenty searches of twenty eight, eight unspent. Most searches blocked the author's own domains so the second source would be independent; four were held to a house's own domain to read its pages (cluver.com, oakvalley.co.za, iona.co.za, shannonwines.com twice), and one search was wasted on a query that returned only general biodynamic pages. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making, label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail stood in one source or none it was cut or hedged as the house's account.

swaps.ruling: none proposed; the author left open whether the Groenlandberg Chardonnay leads. Refused as a swap: the plan's Pinot Noir is kept, since the house sells the two as a pair, the plan's why rests on the district's red side, and the group already holds two Chardonnay flagships (Paul Cluver and Kershaw).

codexTensions: The region record's summary says fruit farmers began planting vines in the 1980s; Oak Valley's own history and Viljoen's cellar of 1907 show wine in Elgin long before, closed in 1944. The summary's modern sense holds, but a reader may meet the older history here. Reported, not edited.

The region record's producers line calls Paul Cluver the family estate that pioneered wine in Elgin in the 1980s; one source credits Oak Valley's experimental block of 1985 as the first planting and Cluver the first commercial one. Reported, not edited.
